nodes.label: What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents
nodes.author: Xingshan Zeng et al.
nodes.rationale: Framework for agentic data generation through Accuracy-Complexity-divErsity (ACE) lens, organizing generation paradigms and verification mechanisms.

nodes.label: Accuracy-Complexity-divErsity (ACE) Framework
nodes.author: Xingshan Zeng et al.
nodes.rationale: Framework for agentic data generation: Accuracy defines valid support, Complexity shapes learning mass relative to learner capability, Diversity ensures non-redundant coverage.

nodes.label: Factorized Agentic Data Object (E, q, τ, v)
nodes.author: Xingshan Zeng et al.
nodes.rationale: Common representation of agentic data: E (environment), q (task), τ (interaction), v (verifier), making consistency relations explicit across domains.

nodes.label: Forward and Reverse Generation Paradigms
nodes.author: Xingshan Zeng et al.
nodes.rationale: Taxonomy of agentic data generation: forward pipelines ground tasks in existing environments; reverse pipelines construct factors around target capabilities or observed experience.

nodes.label: Execution-Grounded Accuracy in Agentic Data
nodes.author: Xingshan Zeng et al.
nodes.rationale: Shift from plausibility judgments toward verification through actual execution, state-based checks, and feedback-based repair in agentic data generation.

nodes.label: Learner-Relative Complexity Calibration
nodes.author: Xingshan Zeng et al.
nodes.rationale: Complexity should be calibrated relative to learner capability and execution configuration, not as static difficulty heuristics.

nodes.label: Behavioral Diversity in Agentic Data
nodes.author: Xingshan Zeng et al.
nodes.rationale: Diversity should expand beyond surface variation toward non-redundant coverage of environments, tasks, and interaction behaviors.

nodes.label: Agentic Data Generation Survey
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive survey on agentic data generation, decomposing the problem into environment specification, task signal, and interaction realization, with ACE (Accuracy, Complexity, Diversity) as the organizing framework.

nodes.label: Agentic Data Decomposition Framework
nodes.rationale: Core conceptual framework: Agentic Data = Environment Specification (E) + Task Signal (q) + Interaction Realization (τ) + optional Verifier (v). This decomposition is central to understanding how agentic data is constructed and evaluated.

nodes.label: ACE Objective: Accuracy, Complexity, Diversity
nodes.rationale: Organizing principle for agentic data generation: Accuracy as admission gate (validity of E, q, τ, v), Complexity calibrated to learner capability, Diversity measuring valid behavioral coverage. Asymmetric: accuracy is prerequisite, complexity and diversity shape utility within valid set.

nodes.label: Forward Generation Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Generation order: Environment → Task → Interaction. Mirrors natural dependency where available actions and states determine feasible tasks and meaningful trajectories. Includes real/curated, LLM-synthesized, and programmatic environment construction.

nodes.label: Reverse Generation Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Alternative generation orders: Task-First (specify capability, construct environment), Trajectory-First (explore/mine workflows, derive tasks), Structure-First (generate intermediate scaffolds like tool graphs, then realize). Offers different control points and consistency recovery mechanisms.

nodes.label: Environment Accuracy
nodes.rationale: Accurate E implements declared tools, states, policies, and transitions consistently. Local checks test schemas and types; global checks test coherent state changes and policy enforcement. Executable environments enable component-level validation before rollout.

nodes.label: Task Accuracy
nodes.rationale: Valid q must be interpretable and feasible under relevant state, tools, and policies. In multi-turn settings, task is often implicit and progressively revealed. Semantic coherence must be maintained over turns unless intentional changes are recognized.

nodes.label: Interaction Accuracy
nodes.rationale: Accurate τ contains schema-compliant actions, causally grounded observations, and behavior consistent with task and policies. Trajectory accuracy is particularly critical as errors in τ are directly imitated by trained models. Filtering procedures remove structurally invalid or semantically inconsistent interactions.

nodes.label: Verifier and Outcome Accuracy
nodes.rationale: Verifier v must correctly recognize successful outcomes, reject meaningful failures, and avoid unintended incentives. Critical for RL where v directly shapes reward signal. Database-backed systems compare states; software-engineering uses tests; formal reasoning uses proof assistants.

nodes.label: Learner-Relative Task Complexity
nodes.rationale: Complexity is model-aware and configuration-dependent (z includes model, scaffold, tools, budget). Useful data occupy learnable band near capability frontier—too easy tasks are redundant, too hard tasks provide no successful trajectory. Band moves as learner improves.

nodes.label: Environment Complexity
nodes.rationale: Burden induced by actionable world: state/action space structure, tool dependencies, transition dynamics, observation protocol, policies, other actors. Large environments not necessarily complex; complexity arises when features create task-relevant alternatives, prerequisites, uncertainty, or consequences.

nodes.label: Task-Signal Complexity
nodes.rationale: Arises from compositional goals, interacting constraints, implicit/progressively revealed intent, cross-source evidence, subgoal dependencies. Distinct from linguistic obscurity; missing information creates complexity only when recoverable from user/environment/tools.

nodes.label: Interaction-Realization Complexity
nodes.rationale: Minimum consequential interaction structure required to solve task in environment. Includes serial dependencies, branching, parallel subgoals, joins, loops, clarification, recovery. Separates task-required interaction from policy-dependent inefficiency.

nodes.label: Environment-Specification Diversity
nodes.rationale: Variation in actionable world: tool/action schemas, initial states, transition dynamics, observation interfaces, policies, modalities, verifiers, other actors. Subdimensions: state, action-space, observation, dynamics, rule, reward diversity. Tool names weak proxy when systems expose same preconditions/effects.

nodes.label: Task-Signal Diversity
nodes.rationale: What agent is asked to achieve: goals/capabilities, interacting constraints, user profiles, intent revelation, feasibility regimes, difficulty bands. Clarification, refusal, partial completion, recovery, successful completion are distinct task regimes, not collapsed into generic hard cases.

nodes.label: Interaction-Realization Diversity
nodes.rationale: For fixed environment and task, multiple valid interaction processes may exist. Covers horizon, turn structure, alternative plans/action orders, tool substitutions, action representations, clarification/recovery patterns, assistance, outcomes. Distinction is behavioral: alternative paths reveal strategy coverage.

nodes.label: POMDP Formulation of Agentic Multi-turn Interaction
nodes.rationale: Models tool-augmented interaction as partially observable Markov decision process: U (task/user-intent space), S (latent state), A (action space with language and environment-facing actions), O (observation), P (state transitions), R (reward/evaluation). Policy acts on observable history; environment maintains latent state.

nodes.label: Environment Parameterization for Data Generation
nodes.rationale: Concrete environment parameterized as: D (state carrier: database, repository, simulator), F (tool/action set), P_rule (policies, permissions, constraints), Ω (observation exposure), v (success interface). Serialized specification E describes some/all components; ranges from static interface specs to complete interaction substrate.

nodes.label: Layered Rule-, Model-, and Human-Based Verification
nodes.rationale: No single verifier detects all failures. Compose checks along cost (inexpensive rules to expensive human review) and granularity (individual actions to complete trajectories). Rules establish structural properties; execution/state test operational consistency; step/trajectory critics examine causal/semantic coherence. Human review as selective escalation.

nodes.label: Constraint-Grounded Construction for Accuracy
nodes.rationale: Restrict what can be generated: verify blueprints before multi-turn simulation, use tool graphs/workflow structures to constrain actions, construct tasks with initial states/rules/success conditions, write tasks from observed executable paths. Structural anchor across E, q, τ, v prevents invalid plans from contaminating later stages.

nodes.label: Execution- and State-Based Verification
nodes.rationale: Ground verification in actual execution rather than plausibility judgments. Generated actions/trajectories executed against tools/environments; effects checked through tool responses, state transitions, tests, formal objectives. Prevents fabrication of observations, produces reproducible failure signals. Incomplete without process checks and semantic review.

nodes.label: Feedback-Based Repair and Selective Admission
nodes.rationale: Verification controls subsequent generation: localize failed tests and regenerate, revise plans before realization, retry from last verified state. Reject/repair at earliest failed stage especially valuable for long trajectories. Preserve alternative valid paths; use failure types to guide targeted regeneration rather than discard.

nodes.label: Structural Specification and Composition for Complexity
nodes.rationale: Specify dependency structure before task realization: construct subgoal graphs, tool-dependency paths, scenario-skill paths, coupled constraints, or initial-to-goal plans. Instantiate tasks requiring selected structure. Depth creates serial dependence, width introduces parallel subgoals, joins require integration, conditional edges make actions state-dependent.

nodes.label: Task and Information Control for Complexity
nodes.rationale: Adjust what must be achieved or initial information availability. Omit from initial request, disclose through user turns, distribute across observations, make discoverable only through tools. Creates clarification, retrieval, state-tracking burdens. Key condition: resolvability—withheld information must have intended source and recovery action.

nodes.label: Environment and Interaction Design for Complexity
nodes.rationale: Change decision process: typed tool dependencies, shared state, persistent databases, policy boundaries, restricted observation protocols create prerequisites/consequences spanning multiple actions. Initial-state selection and controlled information access increase state inference burden. Implementation domain-dependent (coding: dependencies/feedback; embodied: geometry/physics; social: private info/incentives).

nodes.label: Completion and Feedback Design for Complexity
nodes.rationale: Control complexity through success definition: target state, coupled constraints, rubric items, forbidden actions, infeasibility diagnosis. State targets, constraint programs, rubric trees, subgoal evaluators make requirements machine-checkable. Path-centric rewards and step-level checks assign credit to intermediate evidence gathering.

nodes.label: Evolution and Progressive Transformation for Complexity
nodes.rationale: Transform valid seeds rather than generate hard instances from scratch. Progressively remove procedural cues, strengthen goal conditions, extend verified follow-up subtasks, compose workflow-relevant skills, produce longer workflows. Preserves grounded core; makes intended burden source easier to identify. Adaptive variants use execution outcomes to choose transformations.

nodes.label: Failure-Driven and Model-Aware Complexity Calibration
nodes.rationale: Structural controls describe why candidate may be hard; solver behavior determines if informative. Model-aware pipelines estimate verified success under stated model/scaffold/budget, retain candidates near target success band or capability frontier. Capability profiles and observed failures direct generation toward specific weaknesses. Failure informative only after validity established.

nodes.label: Bidirectional Calibration and Scaffolding
nodes.rationale: Complexity control bidirectional: saturated candidates strengthened by adding dependency/reducing information/tightening requirements; beyond-useful candidates simplified by reversing changes or supplying intermediate goals/procedural prerequisites/action hints. Scaffolding changes execution configuration z; comparisons should keep instance fixed and state objective.

nodes.label: Source and Support Expansion for Diversity
nodes.rationale: Add environments, tools, repositories, scenes, users, modalities, task sources, verification regimes. Heterogeneous documents/real traces offer authentic long-tail but inherit imbalance; model generation more controllable but repeats teacher priors; programmatic construction supports execution/reset but may reproduce templates. Nominal scale incomplete measure.

nodes.label: Compositional Recombination for Diversity
nodes.rationale: Create new relations among existing components: multi-tool dependencies, cross-application workflows, interacting user constraints, cross-file edits, multi-object tasks. Graph/blueprint-based pipelines sample compatible components before realization, reducing contradictions. Composition adds diversity only when components interact and change required behavior.

nodes.label: Exploration and Experience-First Discovery for Diversity
nodes.rationale: Traverse environment/simulator/repository/proof system and derive tasks from reachable behavior. Supports tool/GUI interaction, robotics, program discovery, scientific search. Reverse generation from executed combinations grounds tasks in observed evidence. Reachability not guarantee of broad support; multiple policies, external seeds, novelty signals help separate support from discovery.

nodes.label: Perturbation and Counterfactual Variation for Diversity
nodes.rationale: Controlled variation changes selected factors while holding others fixed: initial state, policy, user constraint, observation format, tool semantics, layout, physical parameters. Expose query/action/observation/domain shifts. Matched counterfactuals reveal whether change causes intended effect. Variants altering only surface form add apparent entropy; implausible perturbations leave deployment distribution.

nodes.label: Coverage-Guided Balancing and Adaptation for Diversity
nodes.rationale: Target under-represented factor combinations, remove redundancy, allocate toward named transfer gaps. Model-adaptive pipelines use failures/uncertainty/solve-rate band to produce experience near learner frontier. Self-evolving systems feed behavior/experience/world-model errors into generation. Adaptation improves efficiency but can overfit; coverage constraints and periodic exploration preserve skills.

nodes.label: Factor Coverage and Balance Measurement
nodes.rationale: Divide each factor level into categories. Coverage: fraction of declared categories with ≥1 sample. Normalized entropy: how evenly samples distributed across categories (1=uniform, decreases as concentration increases). Complementary: coverage high even if concentrated; entropy alone doesn't show absent categories. Supplement with meaningful joint distributions.

nodes.label: Behavioral Non-Redundancy Measurement
nodes.rationale: Category coverage overestimates diversity when differently worded samples require same behavior. Compare through tool-call/action graphs, state transitions, dependency paths, clarification/recovery patterns, final-state changes. Graph fingerprints and kernel-based effective-number measures summarize non-redundancy; chosen representation and similarity function must be reported.

nodes.label: Real and Synthetic Data under ACE
nodes.rationale: Real data: direct evidence of authentic interfaces/behavior/needs but may contain failed behavior, hidden context, stale interfaces, privacy issues. Synthetic: explicit states/constraints/verifiers, regenerate failures, but limited by generator fidelity. Neither uniformly better; hybrid allocation: real defines deployment factors and seeds semantics; synthetic expands/balances/calibrates around anchors.

nodes.label: Agentic Pre-training and Mid-training Data Generation
nodes.rationale: Expose models earlier to state transitions, action-observation dependencies, tool composition, persistent policies, long-horizon information seeking. Complete expert rollouts too expensive; motivates executable/learned environments and conversion of repositories/videos/documents into interaction supervision. Training unit need not be complete (E,q,τ,v); local transitions, inverse-dynamics, dependency completions, reachability objectives, distilled knowledge can teach components.

nodes.label: Data Generation for Self-Evolving Agents
nodes.rationale: Change data generation from offline preparation to continual learning loop. Observe agent behavior, identify capability gaps, generate/discover relevant experience, use verified outcomes to guide updates. May create targeted tasks around failures, modify difficulty, explore for new states, repair invalid rollouts, extract skills, replay earlier experience. Central problem: selecting/transforming/allocating experience by expected value for current agent.

nodes.label: Scaling Law under ACE Objective
nodes.rationale: Raw quantity weak proxy for useful scale; additional samples contribute unevenly. Accuracy determines admissible pool; Complexity determines if valid samples informative for learner; Diversity determines if new data expand support or densify existing modes. Relevant scaling variable closer to effective support than dataset size. Scaling can occur by producing more valid experience, moving probability mass toward learner's useful frontier, or expanding coverage.

nodes.label: Tool-Use and Digital Agents Diversity
nodes.rationale: Coverage spans executable state effects, coherent tool dependencies, multi-turn information flow, policies, errors, action representations. Search agents add variation in sources, retrieval engines, decomposition, evidence paths, query revision. Tool identity substantially undercounts behavioral support. Tool-pool and per-task toolset coverage improve OOD performance more efficiently than repeated sampling.

nodes.label: Web, GUI, and Computer-Use Agents Diversity
nodes.rationale: Variation spans applications, layouts, operating systems, modalities, initial states, persistent effects, cross-application workflows. Combine real/recreated interfaces with procedural task generation, reverse synthesis, environment exploration, multimodal actions, recovery traces. Separate visual from behavioral diversity: different screenshots may share interaction topology; small permission/state change may reverse correct action.

nodes.label: Coding and Software-Engineering Agents Diversity
nodes.rationale: Coverage includes languages, repository structures, dependencies, build systems, tests, project histories; task/trajectory coverage include issue types, localization paths, edit scopes, test feedback, recovery. Scale executable repositories and multilingual trajectories, generate feature-level tasks/tests, allocate fixed budgets across distinct trajectory structures. Meaningful unit is verified problem-repository-feedback relation.

nodes.label: Embodied and Social Agents Diversity
nodes.rationale: Embodied: scenes, objects, affordances, physics, sensors, embodiments, action effects. Procedural generation behaviorally useful when scene variation coupled with activities, physical constraints, task graphs, policy changes. Social: partner policies, incentives, private information, communication, institutions. Persona variation alone weak unless factors change transitions/rewards.

nodes.label: Scientific and Formal Agents Diversity
nodes.rationale: Candidate breadth tightly constrained by feasibility/verification. Generative systems explore materials, proteins, hypotheses, experiments, programs, proofs under property predictors, execution, simulation, formal checking. Distinction between candidate diversity and valid discovery diversity explicit: verifier coverage must expand with candidate space.
